newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields consolidate at new lower levels at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields consolidate at new lower levels at close.

text.p: * NZ debt markets consolidate recent gains at close
* Long bond bid held in check by offshore sell-order
* Feb retail trade data adds to picture of slowing economy
New Zealand yields consolidated their recent gains during Wednesday's session to finish almost on their opening levels, with the bonds ending around seven basis points below Tuesday's close.
Dealers said U.S. Consumers Price Index data overnight had added to the bullish tone created by Tuesday's local inflation data, which came in well below market expectations.
In the money market, 90-day bank bills ended a couple of basis points above their Tuesday close as the currency's Trade-Weighted Index slipped to 68.43 from 68.62.
Jim Reardon, senior manager of domestic markets at ANZ Bank, said the market was beginning to stall on profit taking following Tuesday's sharp rally.

He said given where monetary conditions were ahead of the CPI announcement, it seemed most banks were either standing on the sideline in anticipation of a poor result, or were positioned for some easing in conditions.
"The profit taking has essentially soaked up the first wave of buying and we need to move through that profit taking before we will see substantial gains," Reardon said.
He said there had been a significant offshore seller in long bonds during the session.
"I guess that's been one of the reasons why it hasn't rallied more significantly -- despite that selling interest we still seem to have had more buyers."
